a tripodal hexdentate ligand forms an optically active silicon(IV) complex.
the reaction of Si(OCOCH3)4 with a tripodal ligand H3L (1,1, 1-tris(Nsalicylideneaminmethyl)ethane), afforded the colorless six-coordinate [Si(L)] + complex.

a tripodal hexdentate ligand (1,1,3-tris(salicylideneamino)propane) was synthesized, the reaction of the ligand with Si(OCOCH3)4 afforded a colorless [SiL] complex, and the complex was optically resolved by crystallization with (−)-Dibenzoyl-l-tartaric Acid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of new chiral organosilicon compounds, which are of potential interest in the synthesis of new materials and as chiral catalysts for asymmetric organic synthesis.
the synthesis and the characterization of new silicon complexes, which can serve as models for biological systems.

the design and synthesis of new ligands and complexes with the goal of developing a new generation of silicon-based catalysts for the polymerization of polar monomers such as lactide and ε-caprolactone.

the Si–O bonds are shorter than the Si–N bonds in the complex.
the reaction of silicon tetraisopropoxide with the tripodal hexadenti ate ligand afforded the colorless complex [Si(L)]+, which was optically resolved.
the reaction of a six-coordinate silicon(IV) complex with a tripodal ligand with an excess of a chiral resolving agent leads to the formation of an enantiomerically enriched diastereomere salt.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a tripodal ligand with three N-donors and three O-donors is a good chelating ligand for the silicon(IV) ion, and that this complex can be optically resolved.
the complex [Si(L)]+, which is a model compound of the active species in the polymerization of tetrafluoroethylene, is the first six-coordinate silicon(IV) complex with a tripodal ligand.
the Si–O bonds are more polarized than the Si–N bonds, which is in agreement with the electronegativities of oxygen (3.5) and nitrogen (3.0) as well as the Si–N (2.0) and Si–O (1.7) bond polarities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to isolate a stable six-coordinate complex of Si(IV) in which the metal center is bound to a tripodal hexedentate ligand.
the complex can be optically resolved and that the complex is stable toward water.
the Si–O bonds of the complex are significantly stronger than the Si–N bonds.
